sections: Software

Nexwall Firewall is a set of free and open source components and of Nexwall components. The open source components (for example OpenWrt, the Linux kernel, nftables, Snort, dnsmasq, ClamAV, Squid) are licensed under their own licenses, which apply to those components and are listed in the notices of the image. The Nexwall components that are not open source (for example the web interface, the license component and the Web Protection services) are licensed to you under these terms.
Your rights and the limits of the license

You receive a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to install and use the software for your own business or home network, or for the networks of your customers if you are a Nexwall partner. You may not remove license notices, circumvent, disable or tamper with license checks, usage counting or updates, resell or sublicense the Nexwall components, use them to build a competing product, or reverse engineer them except where the law allows it regardless of this restriction. Use is limited to what your license, subscription or trial allows.
Trial, subscriptions and modules

The image includes a trial period. After it, the licensed features and modules need a subscription that you obtain from Nexwall or from a Nexwall partner, and the Services Agreement applies to it. Features that are not licensed keep working as the product describes, with the limits stated in the release notes.
Release candidates and test versions

Versions marked as release candidates or test versions are for evaluation and testing. They are provided as they are, without warranty and without support, and are not meant for production networks without an agreement with Nexwall.
Your responsibilities

You decide how the software is configured and used, and you are responsible for: the rules, profiles and policies you create; the protection of passwords, keys and certificates; backups of your configuration and data; testing changes and updates before using them in a production network; the lawful use of the software, including having the right and the consent needed to inspect the traffic, the encrypted (HTTPS) traffic and the files of the users of your network; and the third-party services you connect to it. The software is not designed for uses where a failure could cause death, injury or serious damage (for example medical, aviation or nuclear systems); if you use it that way, you do so at your own risk.
Security protection has limits

No security product detects or blocks every threat or every attack. Nexwall does not promise that the software or the services will be uninterrupted, error free, completely secure or suited to your particular needs, or that they will find, stop or prevent every threat, intrusion, malware, data loss or misuse. They can block something that is harmless (false positive) or let something harmful pass (false negative). Advanced and Collective Protection (AI) gives probabilistic, advisory scores, is trained in a laboratory and is not a guarantee of detection, including of unknown (zero-day) threats. Threat lists and categories come in part from third parties and open sources that Nexwall does not control. Security is a shared responsibility and you must keep your own layers of protection.
Ownership and feedback

The software, the services, the data and the materials of Nexwall, and their improvements, belong to Nexwall and its licensors; you receive only the rights stated here. You keep the ownership of your own data and configuration. If you send suggestions or feedback, Nexwall may use them freely and without payment.
Updates and changes

Nexwall may update, change, replace or discontinue features, modules, feeds, models and versions, and publishes the lifecycle of each version. Updates are signed and some are installed automatically as you configure. Nexwall may change these terms by publishing the new version; if the change is material and affects you, Nexwall will tell you in advance when it is practical. If you keep using the software after the change takes effect, you accept it; if you do not accept it, stop using the software.
License checks and usage

The software contacts the Nexwall license service to check and renew the license and to receive updates, and it can report technical data about the use (for example the version, the licensed modules and the number of devices or users) to verify the license. Using more than the license includes is not a reason for the protection to stop; Nexwall may ask you to adjust the license. The Privacy Notice explains what is processed.
Software provided as is (no warranty)

To the maximum extent permitted by law, the software, the licenses, the modules and the services are provided "as is" and "as available", whether you paid for them or received them free of charge, and Nexwall, its partners and suppliers give no warranty of any kind, express or implied, including of merchantability, of fitness for a particular purpose, of non-infringement, of accuracy, of availability or of results. Warranties that the law does not allow to be excluded are not excluded.
Liability

To the maximum extent permitted by law, and whether you paid for the software, a license, a module or a service or received it free of charge, Nexwall, its partners, suppliers, licensors and staff are not liable for any loss or damage of any kind that arises from or is related to the software, the licenses, the modules, the services or their use or inability to use, direct or indirect, including loss of profit, revenue, business, data or goodwill, interruption of business, the cost of replacement, a security incident, or a threat that was not detected or a legitimate use that was blocked, under any legal theory (contract, tort, negligence or any other) and even if Nexwall was told that the loss was possible. Where the law does not allow a full exclusion, the total liability of Nexwall is limited, to the maximum extent permitted by law, to the amount you paid for the affected license or subscription in the 3 months before the event, and it is zero for anything you received free of charge. privacy.title: Privacy Notice
privacy.updated: Version 2026-10 · Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD, Law 13.709/2018)
sections: Who is the controller

The controller of the personal data processed on this page is {controller}. The data protection officer (encarregado, article 41 of the LGPD) {dpo}. Use this contact for any request or question about your data.
What we collect

When you ask for a download we collect: first name, last name, company and email address (required); corporate phone or WhatsApp number (optional); the version and file you asked for; the date and time of the request and of the downloads; the IP address and the type of browser (access logs). We do not collect sensitive personal data. This page uses no tracking or advertising cookies.
What we use it for and the legal basis

1. To give you the download and a time-limited link, at your request: preliminary procedures at the request of the data subject (article 7, V). 2. To contact you, by email or phone, if there is a problem with the download or an export compliance or licensing question: legitimate interest (article 7, IX) and compliance with a legal or regulatory obligation (article 7, II). 3. To protect the service from abuse and fraud, using the IP address and the browser type: legitimate interest (article 7, IX). 4. To keep the application access logs: compliance with a legal obligation (Marco Civil da Internet, article 15). 5. To contact you by email, phone or WhatsApp about support, licenses and Nexwall commercial matters: only with your consent (article 7, I), given by accepting the form and which you can withdraw at any time.
Who we share it with

Only with Nexwall staff who need the data and with processors that handle it on our behalf and under our instructions (for example the hosting of the service). We do not sell personal data. We may share it with authorities when the law requires it.
Where the data is
The data is kept on servers located in Brazil. If it is ever transferred to another country, this will happen only in the cases of article 33 of the LGPD and you will be informed.
How long we keep it

The form data is kept for 24 months from your last download request, or until you ask us to delete it. Access logs (IP address, date and time) are kept for 6 months, as article 15 of the Marco Civil da Internet requires. We may keep data longer to comply with a legal obligation, to exercise rights in proceedings or, anonymised, for statistics (article 16 of the LGPD).
Your rights

Under article 18 of the LGPD you can, at any time and by a request to the data protection officer: confirm that we process your data; access it; correct incomplete, inaccurate or outdated data; ask for anonymisation, blocking or deletion of unnecessary data or data processed in breach of the law; ask for portability; ask for deletion of data processed with your consent; know who we share it with; know that you may refuse consent and what follows; and withdraw consent. We answer within 15 days (article 19). You can also complain to the Brazilian data protection authority (ANPD).
Security
The page uses an encrypted connection, access to the data is limited to authorised people and protected by a password, and download links expire after 24 hours.
Children and teenagers
The service is meant for professionals and companies. We do not knowingly collect data from children and teenagers.
Reports shared by the firewall (Collective Protection)

Firewalls with Advanced and Collective Protection (AI) can send reports about suspicious external addresses and domains. Switch: on by default, can be switched off at any time on the Advanced and Collective Protection (AI) page. What is sent: the external address or domain, the kind of behaviour, a score, the date and the identity of the firewall (a device token and a signature). What is never sent: the content of traffic, files, user names, internal addresses, browsing history. Purpose: to protect all customers, by publishing an indicator when at least 3 different firewalls reported it or when the Nexwall team confirmed it; published indicators expire after 14 days. Legal basis: legitimate interest in network security (LGPD article 7, IX) and fraud prevention and security of the holder (article 11, II, g, where applicable). Reports are kept on servers in Brazil for as long as the indicator is valid and up to 12 months for the review history. Contact the data protection officer for any request.
Changes to this notice
If we change this notice we publish the new version here with its date. Changes that affect the purpose or the consent will be communicated to you beforehand.

sections: Scope and acceptance

This agreement is between you (the customer) and {controller} ("Nexwall") and applies to the subscriptions and the online services of Nexwall Firewall: the license service, the signed update feeds (application categories, intrusion prevention rules, DNS and IP and country lists, threat lists), the Web Protection services (website categories, antivirus signatures, YARA rules and sandbox), the models and the indicator service of Advanced and Collective Protection (AI), software updates and support. It is read together with the End User Terms of Use and the Privacy Notice. You accept it when you activate a license or a subscription, when you use the services, or when you accept it in a proposal or an order. If you buy through a Nexwall partner, the partner sets the price and the payment with you and this agreement applies to the services.

The subscription states the modules, the number of devices, users or firewalls (the entitlement) and the term. You may use the services only within the entitlement and for your own information security, or for your customers if you are a partner. If you use more than the entitlement, Nexwall may ask you to adjust the subscription and to pay for the extra use; the protection that is working is not stopped for this reason.

The fees are those of the proposal, the order or the price list at the time of purchase. Purchases made directly from Nexwall are paid by the date on the invoice, or in 30 days if it does not say otherwise. For a late payment the law allows a fine of 2% and interest of 1% per month plus monetary correction. The fees do not include taxes, which are due by you where the law says so. Purchases made through a partner are paid to the partner.
Term, renewal and cancellation

The subscription runs for the term of the order. It renews for the same period unless you or Nexwall give notice that it will not, in the way and at the time that the order or the site states. Fees already paid are not refunded, except where the law requires it or this agreement says so. If you are a consumer and you bought at a distance, you have the right to withdraw within 7 days of the purchase, under article 49 of the Consumer Defense Code.

Nexwall works to keep the services available but does not guarantee any level of availability, speed or response time, except one that is agreed in writing in an order. The services may be interrupted for maintenance, updates, emergencies, third-party failures or events outside the control of Nexwall. When a service cannot be reached, the firewall keeps working with the last data that it received. Support is given as the plan or the order says and, for products given free of charge, only through the public documentation.

Nexwall may improve, change, replace or remove services, feeds, categories, models and indicators, as the threats and the technology change. If a change reduces a paid service in a material way during the term, you may end the subscription and receive a refund of the unused part.

The Privacy Notice explains the data that the services process. Nexwall does not receive the content of your traffic. Advanced and Collective Protection (AI) can send reports about suspicious external addresses and domains; the switch is on by default and you can turn it off at any time on that page. An indicator reported by at least 3 different firewalls within 14 days is published to all firewalls, and one reported by a single firewall is published only after the Nexwall team confirms it; indicators expire after 14 days without new reports. A published indicator does not identify you. You agree that Nexwall uses these reports, and anonymised technical and threat data, to protect all customers and to improve its products.
